question: Does iterative decompression correctness (byte-identical output to ground-truth uncompressed body) hold for gzip multi-chunk transfer encoding on a localhost mock server with auth-aware caching?
hypothesis: Iterative decompression (gzip->identity, max_depth=5) produces byte-identical output to ground-truth generate_*_body(state, target_size) for all 4 auth states across 3 content types (JSON/HTML/XML) at 1KB nominal with gzip multi-chunk framing (chunk_size=32 bytes).
falsifier: Any SHA256(decompressed) != SHA256(generate_*_body(state, target_size)) across all 240 gzip observations, OR any silent fallback (SHA256(decompressed) == SHA256(raw_compressed)) for gzip-compressed responses.

baselines.description: Brotli multi-chunk correctness (established 360/360 in parent EXP-RUNTIME-35456070671)
baselines.expected: 100% correctness, serves as positive control for decompression pipeline integrity

baselines.description: IDENTITY (no compression) baseline—hash matches generate_*_body() exactly
Gzip single-chunk (chunk_size=1024)—tests gzip correctness without chunk-boundary stress
baselines.expected: 100% correctness; if gzip SC passes but MC fails, chunk boundaries are the failure mode

positive_control: BROTLI-MC (brotli multi-chunk): established 360/360 in parent; must pass 100% to confirm no regression in decompression pipeline infrastructure.
null_control: B-RANDOM: Within-state decompressed hash must be deterministic (all_same=true for all 4 auth states across all gzip cells). Any within-state hash variation indicates non-deterministic decompression or server behavior.
measurement_validity: Correctness oracle validated: generate_*_body(state, target_size) produces byte-identical output to uncompressed server responses (established via IDENTITY baseline in parent)
Deterministic server: Flask mock with seeded RNG (seed=44) produces deterministic bodies per (state, content_type) pair
Silent fallback detection: SHA256(decompressed) == SHA256(raw_compressed) classified as failure, not success
Gzip compression at quality-level equivalent (compressionlevel=6 for brotli, default for gzip) to match parent's compression intensity
chunk_size=32 for multi-chunk to stress chunk-boundary handling (gzip compressed 1KB payloads typically 300-600 bytes, spanning 10-19 chunks at 32 bytes)
Max decompression depth 5 (gzip->identity is depth 1; no multi-layer encoding in this design)
Request jitter 50-150ms uniform between requests to avoid rate-limit effects
Python 3.12 stdlib gzip module (no external dependencies)
decision_rule: SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST requires ALL of: (C1) correctness_match_rate == 1.0 for ALL 12 gzip cells (4 states x 3 content types x 1 chunk mode); (C2) silent_fallback_count == 0 for ALL gzip cells; (C3) B-BROTLI-MC passes 100% (no regression); (C4) null_control passes (all_same=true for all states in all gzip cells). FALSIFIED if any correctness failure OR any silent fallback in gzip cells. MEASUREMENT_INVALID if infrastructure prevents data collection.
product_consequence_positive: Gzip decompression correctness validated under chunked transfer encoding. Combined with established brotli correctness, the iterative decompression pipeline covers both major content-encoding formats. C-MEAS-VALID advances toward product readiness for the decompression correctness gate.
product_consequence_negative: Gzip decompression fails under chunked framing. The iterative decompression pipeline is encoding-specific, not general. Product cannot ship gzip decompression without diagnosis. The decompression implementation requires investigation of gzip-specific chunk-boundary handling.
estimated_cost: Low: ~240 HTTP requests to localhost mock server, <2 minutes execution, no external infrastructure, no API costs
expected_information_gain: High: fills the specific gzip unknown from the parent handoff; determines whether the decompression pipeline generalizes beyond brotli; a negative result changes the product shipping scope; a positive result removes the last common-encoding blocker for C-MEAS-VALID decompression correctness
